assumptions.condition: The law of \(N\) is invariant under time shifts.
\(G(A)\) contains no directed cycle, with a self-loop counted as a directed cycle of length one.

novel.justification: This contribution-defining restriction describes labeled feed-forward alarm cascades along documented access, aggregation, and core-network dependencies, where propagation is modeled over a window short enough that slower remediation feedback is external to the Hawkes mechanism. Because self-loops are admissible in \(G(A)\) before the restriction is imposed, acyclicity itself forces \(A_{ii}=0\).

This identification-specific exclusion is necessary because \(A=0\) yields independent homogeneous Poisson coordinates whose observable law is unchanged for every \(\beta>0\), as characterized separately in \(\text{prop:empty-graph-equivalence}\). It is appropriate for scientific windows selected to contain at least one reproducible cross-label excitation channel.

definitions.name: Acyclic common-decay closure class
definitions.construction: \(\overline{\mathcal M}_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG}}=\{P_{N,\mu,\beta,A}:p\geq2,\ \Delta>0,\ N\text{ is stationary with the stated exponential Hawkes intensity},\ \mu_i>0,\ \beta>0,\ A_{ij}\geq0,\ G(A)\text{ contains no directed cycle under the convention that a self-loop is a cycle of length one, for every }i,j\in\{1,\ldots,p\}\}\).

definitions.name: Nonempty acyclic common-decay class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG},+}=\{P_{N,\mu,\beta,A}:P_{N,\mu,\beta,A}\text{ satisfies every member property of }\overline{\mathcal M}_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG}}\text{ and }A\neq0\text{ for every }p\geq2\text{ and }\Delta>0\}\).

definitions.name: Fixed conditioning-margin class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)=\{P_{N,\mu,\beta,A}:P_{N,\mu,\beta,A}\text{ satisfies every member property of }\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG},+},\ \sigma_r(\Gamma_1)\geq\kappa,\ e^{-\beta\Delta}\in[\kappa,1-\kappa],\ \beta+\lVert\mu\rVert_2+\lVert A\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\kappa^{-1},\ \min_i\lambda_i\geq\kappa,\ \lambda_{\min}\{\Omega(\theta)\}\geq\kappa,\ \min_{i\neq j:Z_{ij}\neq0}|Z_{ij}|\geq\kappa\text{ for every }i,j\in\{1,\ldots,p\},\ p\geq2,\text{ and }\Delta>0\}\).

definitions.name: Nuisance-regular acyclic closure class
definitions.construction: \(\overline{\mathcal M}_{\Delta,p}(\kappa_0)=\{P_{N,\mu,\beta,A}:P_{N,\mu,\beta,A}\text{ satisfies every member property of }\overline{\mathcal M}_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG}},\ e^{-\beta\Delta}\in[\kappa_0,1-\kappa_0],\ \beta+\lVert\mu\rVert_2+\lVert A\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\kappa_0^{-1},\ \min_{1\leq i\leq p}\lambda_i\geq\kappa_0,\ \lambda_{\min}\{\Omega(\theta)\}\geq\kappa_0\text{ for every }p\geq2\text{ and }\Delta>0\}\).

definitions.name: Fixed-bin mean and lag covariances
definitions.construction: \(X_k=N(((k+1)\Delta))-N(k\Delta),\quad m=\mathbb E[X_0],\quad\Gamma_k=\mathbb E[(X_k-m)(X_0-m)^{\mathsf T}]\) for every \(k\geq0\).

definitions.name: Basis-invariant two-lag inverse
definitions.construction: For \(r=\operatorname{rank}(\Gamma_1)>0\), choose any orthonormal \(O\) spanning \(S=\operatorname{im}(\Gamma_1)\), set \(R=O^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_1\), \(F=O^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_2R^{\mathsf T}(RR^{\mathsf T})^{-1}\), \(q=\operatorname{tr}(F)/r\), \(\beta^\star=-\Delta^{-1}\log q\), \(E=q^{-1}F-I_r\), \(L^\star=-\beta^\star I_r+\Delta^{-1}\sum_{h=1}^{r-1}(-1)^{h+1}E^h/h\), \(H^\star=L^\star(F-I_r)^{-1}\), \(K^\star=O(H^\star)^2R\), \(Z^\star=K^\star-(K^\star)^{\mathsf T}\), \(\lambda^\star=m/\Delta\), \(A_{ii}^\star=0\), \(A_{ij}^\star=\max\{Z_{ij}^\star,0\}/\lambda_j^\star\) for \(i\neq j\), and \(\mu^\star=(I_p-A^\star/\beta^\star)\lambda^\star\); define \(\Phi_{\Delta,r}(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)=(\beta^\star,A^\star,\mu^\star)\).

definitions.name: Covariance-only inverse
definitions.construction: Apply the transition and logarithm steps of \(\Phi_{\Delta,r}\) to \((\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\), form \(\widetilde C_{+}(t)=Oe^{L^\star t}(H^\star)^2R\), set \(D^\star=\Delta^{-1}[\Gamma_0-\int_0^\Delta(\Delta-t)\{\widetilde C_{+}(t)+\widetilde C_{+}(t)^{\mathsf T}\}\,dt]\), set \(\lambda^\star=\operatorname{diag}(D^\star)\), and complete the edge and baseline steps of \(\Phi_{\Delta,r}\); the output is \(\Psi_{\Delta,r}(\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\).

definitions.name: Raw-moment centering map
definitions.construction: For \(\xi=(m,\operatorname{vec}(M_1),\operatorname{vec}(M_2))\), set \(\mathcal C(\xi)=(m,M_1-mm^{\mathsf T},M_2-mm^{\mathsf T})=(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)=\eta\).

definitions.name: Rank-adaptive moment inverse
definitions.construction: Set \(\widehat\xi_n=(n-2)^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{n-3}Y_k\), \(\widehat\eta_n=\mathcal C(\widehat\xi_n)=(\widehat m_n,\widehat\Gamma_{1,n},\widehat\Gamma_{2,n})\), and \(\widehat r_n=\sum_{s=1}^p\mathbf1\{\sigma_s(\widehat\Gamma_{1,n})>t_n\}\). Use a fixed Borel-measurable singular-value-decomposition rule to choose the truncated left singular subspace and its orthonormal basis. For \(\widehat r_n>0\), compute every starred intermediate in \(\text{def:two-lag-inverse}\), and let \(\mathcal V_n\) be the event that \(\sigma_{\widehat r_n}(\widehat\Gamma_{1,n})>\sigma_{\widehat r_n+1}(\widehat\Gamma_{1,n})\), with \(\sigma_{p+1}=0\), the resulting \(q\) lies in \((0,1)\), every inverse in that definition exists, every component of \(\lambda^\star=\widehat m_n/\Delta\) used as a divisor is positive, and \(I_p-A^\star/\beta^\star\) is invertible; declare \(\mathcal V_n\) false when \(\widehat r_n=0\). Set \(\widehat\theta_n=\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}(\mathcal C(\widehat\xi_n))\) on \(\mathcal V_n\), and set the measurable sentinel \(\widehat\theta_n=(1,0,\mathbf1_p)\) on \(\mathcal V_n^c\). When \(\widehat r_n=0\), report the empty graph and leave \(\beta\) set-valued over \((0,\infty)\); when \(\widehat r_n>0\) but \(\mathcal V_n\) fails, report abstention. The sentinel is used only to make every numerical random object total.

definitions.name: Lag-window and composite plug-in covariance estimators
definitions.construction: For the Bartlett kernel \(w(x)=(1-|x|)_+\), set \(\overline Y_n=(n-2)^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{n-3}Y_k=\widehat\xi_n\) and \(\widehat\Omega_n=\widehat\Xi_0+\sum_{h=1}^{b_n}w(h/b_n)(\widehat\Xi_h+\widehat\Xi_h^{\mathsf T})\), where \(\widehat\Xi_h=(n-2)^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{n-h-3}(Y_k-\overline Y_n)(Y_{k+h}-\overline Y_n)^{\mathsf T}\), with an empty inner sum interpreted as zero. This Bartlett matrix is positive semidefinite for every sample. On \(\mathcal V_n\), define \(\widehat W_n=D(\zeta\circ\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}\circ\mathcal C)_{\widehat\xi_n}\widehat\Omega_nD(\zeta\circ\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}\circ\mathcal C)_{\widehat\xi_n}^{\mathsf T}\), evaluating the derivative through the smooth representative \(Z^\star=K^\star-(K^\star)^{\mathsf T}\) before positive parts, and set \(\widehat W_n=0\) on \(\mathcal V_n^c\). Define the measurable event \(\mathcal D_n=\mathcal V_n\cap\{Z_{ij}^\star\neq0\text{ for every }1\leq i<j\leq p\}\). On \(\mathcal D_n\), define \(\widehat V_n=D(\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}\circ\mathcal C)_{\widehat\xi_n}\widehat\Omega_nD(\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}\circ\mathcal C)_{\widehat\xi_n}^{\mathsf T}\); on \(\mathcal D_n^c\), set \(\widehat V_n=0\) as a numerical placeholder. The optional \(\widehat V_n\) is not used to define \(\widehat W_n\) or any graph interval.

definitions.name: Fixed-margin graph and parameter confidence sets
definitions.construction: On \(\mathcal V_n\), let \(\widehat z\) be the vector of upper-triangular entries of the recovered signed jump \(Z^\star=K^\star-(K^\star)^{\mathsf T}\); on \(\mathcal V_n^c\), set \(\widehat z=0\). With the sentinel in \(\text{def:rank-adaptive-estimator}\), this gives the total identity \(\widehat z=\zeta(\widehat\theta_n)\). Let \(\widehat W_n\) be the total positive-semidefinite signed-score covariance in \(\text{def:hac-estimator}\). Conditional on \(\widehat W_n\), for \(\mathcal Z\sim\mathcal N(0,\widehat W_n)\), including singular \(\widehat W_n\), define \(c_{n,1-\alpha}=\inf\{x\in[0,\infty):P(\max_{i<j}|\mathcal Z_{ij}|\leq x\mid\widehat W_n)\geq1-\alpha\}\), with \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\). On \(\mathcal V_n\), set \(I_{ij,n}=[\widehat z_{ij}-c_{n,1-\alpha}/\sqrt n,\widehat z_{ij}+c_{n,1-\alpha}/\sqrt n]\), and let \(\mathcal C_n(1-\alpha)\) be the set of labeled acyclic graphs which, for every \(i<j\), use no edge only if \(0\in I_{ij,n}\), use \(j\to i\) only if \(I_{ij,n}\cap(0,\infty)\neq\varnothing\), and use \(i\to j\) only if \(I_{ij,n}\cap(-\infty,0)\neq\varnothing\). On \(\mathcal V_n^c\), set every \(I_{ij,n}=\mathbb R\) and let \(\mathcal C_n(1-\alpha)\) be the set of all labeled acyclic graphs. Define \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{fm}}(1-\alpha)\) as the full-parameter Wald ellipsoid only on \(\mathcal D_n\) when \(\widehat V_n\) makes that ellipsoid well defined; on every other sample set \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{fm}}(1-\alpha)=\overline\Theta_{\Delta,p}\). This optional parameter benchmark is not used in signed-edge or graph coverage.

definitions.name: Parameter and binned-law topologies
definitions.construction: Set \(\overline\Theta_{\Delta,p}=\{(\beta,A,\mu):P_{\beta,A,\mu}\in\overline{\mathcal M}_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG}}\}\) and \(\Theta_{\Delta,p}^{+}=\{\theta\in\overline\Theta_{\Delta,p}:A\neq0\}\). Equip \(\overline\Theta_{\Delta,p}\) with \(\rho_{\Theta}(\theta,\theta')=1\wedge\{|\beta-\beta'|+\lVert A-A'\rVert_{\mathrm F}+\lVert\mu-\mu'\rVert_2\}\), and equip the induced binned laws with \(\rho_{\mathrm{law}}(P,P')=\sum_{h=1}^{\infty}2^{-h}\{1\wedge\lVert P_{(X_0,\ldots,X_{h-1})}-P'_{(X_0,\ldots,X_{h-1})}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\}\).

definitions.name: One-lag observable, fiber, and three-node support strata
definitions.construction: For \(\theta\in\Theta_{\Delta,p}^{+}\), set \(\mathcal O_1(\theta)=(m(\theta),\Gamma_1(\theta))\) and \(\mathfrak F_1(o)=\{\theta'\in\Theta_{\Delta,p}^{+}:\mathcal O_1(\theta')=o\}\). Let \(\mathfrak G_3^{\mathrm{cfd}}\) contain every labeling of the three-node chain, fork, and diamond motifs. For \(G_0\in\mathfrak G_3^{\mathrm{cfd}}\), set \(\Theta_{s,G_0}=\{\theta\in\Theta_{\Delta,3}^{+}:G(A)=G_0,\ \operatorname{rank}(\Gamma_1(\theta))=s\}\). A subset \(U\subseteq\Theta_{s,G_0}\) is relatively open exactly when \(U=V\cap\Theta_{s,G_0}\) for some \(\rho_{\Theta}\)-open \(V\subseteq\Theta_{\Delta,3}^{+}\).

definitions.name: One-lag compatibility-fiber handle
definitions.construction: For each \(G_0\in\mathfrak G_3^{\mathrm{cfd}}\), eliminate \((\beta,A,\mu)\) from the polynomial-exponential equations defining \(\mathfrak F_1\{\mathcal O_1(\theta)\}\); apply real-algebraic stratification within each \(\Theta_{s,G_0}\), enforce Hawkes positivity, and compare distinct surviving parameters in \(\rho_{\mathrm{law}}\).

definitions.name: Boundary separation and adaptation frontier
definitions.construction: For \(r(\theta)=\operatorname{rank}(\Gamma_1(\theta))\), set \(\delta(\theta)=0\) when \(A=0\), and otherwise set \(\delta(\theta)=1\wedge\sigma_{r(\theta)}(\Gamma_1(\theta))\wedge\min_{i\neq j:Z_{ij}(\theta)\neq0}|Z_{ij}(\theta)|\). Inside \(\overline{\mathcal M}_{\Delta,p}(\kappa_0)\), let \(\mathcal M_{\kappa_0}(\delta)=\{P_{\theta}\in\overline{\mathcal M}_{\Delta,p}(\kappa_0):\delta(\theta)\geq\delta\}\). For \(\mathfrak U_n=(\mathcal G_n,\mathcal T_n)\in\mathfrak H_{n,\kappa_0}(\alpha)\), define \(R_{G,n,\kappa_0}(\delta)=\inf_{\mathfrak U_n\in\mathfrak H_{n,\kappa_0}(\alpha)}\sup_{P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\kappa_0}(\delta)}\mathbb E_{\theta}[\ell_{\mathrm{inc}}(\mathcal G_n,G(A))]\) and \(R_{\Theta,n,\kappa_0}(\delta)=\inf_{\mathfrak U_n\in\mathfrak H_{n,\kappa_0}(\alpha)}\sup_{P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\kappa_0}(\delta)}\mathbb E_{\theta}[\operatorname{diam}_{\Theta}(\mathcal T_n)]\); the focal frontier is \(\mathfrak R_{n,\kappa_0}(\delta)=(R_{G,n,\kappa_0}(\delta),R_{\Theta,n,\kappa_0}(\delta))\).

definitions.name: Rank-boundary confidence-union handle
definitions.construction: Within \(\overline{\mathcal M}_{\Delta,p}(\kappa_0)\), construct contiguous local experiments for the raw-moment process \(Y\) along sequences indexed by \(\delta_n=\delta(\theta_n)\), while keeping the decay, parameter-envelope, intensity, long-run-variance, derived mixing, derived moment, and bandwidth conditions regular. Derive matching lower and upper bounds for \(\mathfrak R_{n,\kappa_0}(\delta_n)\) under \(\ell_{\mathrm{inc}}\) and \(\operatorname{diam}_{\Theta}\), and invert rank-indexed signed-score tests without first selecting one rank.

definitions.name: Stable common-exponential Hawkes class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{stab}}=\{P_{N,\mu,\beta,A}:p\geq2,\ \Delta>0,\ N\text{ is stationary with the stated common-exponential Hawkes intensity},\ \mu_i>0,\ \beta>0,\ A_{ij}\geq0\text{ for every }i,j\in\{1,\ldots,p\},\ \rho(A/\beta)<1\}\), where \(\rho\) denotes spectral radius. No acyclicity, zero-diagonal, orientation, or full-rank condition is part of this class definition.

definitions.name: Full-rank stable no-alias population moment image
definitions.construction:
Let \(\mathfrak I_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{fr}}\) be the population moment image
\[
 \left\{(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2):\begin{array}{l}
 \text{there exists }(\beta,A,\mu)\text{ inducing a law in }\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{stab}},\\
 \det(A)\neq0,\quad
 \operatorname{spec}\{\Delta(A-\beta I_p)\}\subset\{z\in\mathbb C:|\operatorname{Im}z|<\pi\},\\
 \text{and }m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2\text{ are that law's population moments}
 \end{array}\right\}.
\]
This is an image-defined domain, not an additional observable assumption.

definitions.name: Domain-restricted full-rank stable two-lag inverse
definitions.construction:
For \(\eta=(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\in\mathfrak I_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{fr}}\), set
\[
 \lambda^\dagger=m/\Delta,\quad D^\dagger=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda^\dagger),\quad
 T^\dagger=\Gamma_2\Gamma_1^{-1},\quad
 B^\dagger=\Delta^{-1}\operatorname{Log}(T^\dagger),
\]
\[
 J^\dagger=(B^\dagger)^{-1}(T^\dagger-I_p),\quad
 K^\dagger=(J^\dagger)^{-2}\Gamma_1,\quad
 Q^\dagger=\int_0^\infty e^{B^\dagger u}D^\dagger e^{(B^\dagger)^{\mathsf T}u}\,du,
\]
and
\[
 s^\dagger=p^{-1}\operatorname{tr}\!\left\{K^\dagger(Q^\dagger)^{-1}+(B^\dagger)^2\right\},\quad
 \beta^\dagger=(s^\dagger)^{1/2},\quad
 A^\dagger=B^\dagger+\beta^\dagger I_p,\quad
 \mu^\dagger=(I_p-A^\dagger/\beta^\dagger)\lambda^\dagger,
\]
where the square root is the positive real square root. Define the domain-restricted map
\[
 \Phi^{\mathrm{fr}}_{\Delta,p}:\mathfrak I_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{fr}}\longrightarrow
 \mathbb R_+\times\mathbb R^{p\times p}\times\mathbb R^p,
 \qquad
 \Phi^{\mathrm{fr}}_{\Delta,p}(\eta)=(\beta^\dagger,A^\dagger,\mu^\dagger).
\]

definitions.name: Positive-rank zero-diagonal restricted-no-alias population moment image
definitions.construction:
Let \(\mathfrak I_{\Delta,p}^{0,+,\mathrm{rs}}\) be the population moment image
\[
 \left\{(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2):\begin{array}{l}
 \text{there exists }(\beta,A,\mu)\text{ inducing a law in }\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{stab}},\\
 A\neq0,\quad \operatorname{diag}(A)=0,\\
 \operatorname{spec}\!\left(\left.\Delta(A-\beta I_p)\right|_{\operatorname{im}(A)}\right)
 \subset\{z\in\mathbb C:|\operatorname{Im}z|<\pi\},\\
 \text{and }m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2\text{ are that law's population moments}
 \end{array}\right\}.
\]
The restriction is well defined because \(\operatorname{im}(A)\) is invariant under \(A-\beta I_p\).  This is an image-defined domain; it does not require \(A\) to be invertible, acyclic, or free of reciprocal pairs, and it does not encode a recovered parameter as an observable premise.

definitions.name: Domain-restricted singular-feedback two-lag inverse
definitions.construction:
For \(\eta=(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\in\mathfrak I_{\Delta,p}^{0,+,\mathrm{rs}}\), set
\[
 r=\operatorname{rank}(\Gamma_1),\quad S=\operatorname{im}(\Gamma_1),
\]
choose any \(O\in\mathbb R^{p\times r}\) with \(O^{\mathsf T}O=I_r\) and \(\operatorname{im}(O)=S\), and define
\[
 R=O^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_1,\quad
 F=O^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_2R^{\mathsf T}(RR^{\mathsf T})^{-1},
\]
\[
 \lambda^\sharp=m/\Delta,\quad D^\sharp=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda^\sharp),
 \quad L^\sharp=\Delta^{-1}\operatorname{Log}(F),
\]
\[
 \beta^\sharp=-\operatorname{tr}(L^\sharp)/r,\quad
 A_S^\sharp=L^\sharp+\beta^\sharp I_r,\quad
 H^\sharp=L^\sharp(F-I_r)^{-1},
\]
\[
 K^\sharp=O(H^\sharp)^2R,\quad
 Z^\sharp=K^\sharp-(K^\sharp)^{\mathsf T},\quad
 P^\sharp=OO^{\mathsf T},\quad
 W^\sharp=O^{\mathsf T}(D^\sharp)^{-1}O,
\]
\[
 \mathsf C^\sharp=
 \{OA_S^\sharp-Z^\sharp(I_p-P^\sharp)(D^\sharp)^{-1}O\}
 (W^\sharp)^{-1}O^{\mathsf T}+Z^\sharp(I_p-P^\sharp),
\]
and
\[
 A^\sharp=\mathsf C^\sharp(D^\sharp)^{-1},\quad
 \mu^\sharp=(I_p-A^\sharp/\beta^\sharp)\lambda^\sharp.
\]
Define the domain-restricted map
\[
 \Phi_{\Delta,p}^{0,+,\mathrm{rs}}:\mathfrak I_{\Delta,p}^{0,+,\mathrm{rs}}
 \longrightarrow\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb R^{p\times p}\times\mathbb R^p,
 \quad
 \Phi_{\Delta,p}^{0,+,\mathrm{rs}}(\eta)
 =(\beta^\sharp,A^\sharp,\mu^\sharp).
\]

statements.statement: For every law in \(\overline{\mathcal M}_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG}}\), \(Q\succ0\), \(C_{+}(t)=e^{Bt}K\) for \(t>0\), \(K=A(2\beta I_p-A)Q\), \(K-K^{\mathsf T}=AD-DA^{\mathsf T}\), and \(\Gamma_k=T^{k-1}J^2K\) for every \(k\geq1\). Moreover, \(\operatorname{im}(\Gamma_1)=\operatorname{im}(K)=\operatorname{im}(A)\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(\Gamma_1)=\operatorname{rank}(A)\), including singular, disconnected, repeated-pole, diamond, and proportional-row cases.
statements.justification: This identity is the algebraic compression that turns a full covariance function into an observable finite-dimensional semigroup without assuming \(A\) invertible.
statements.gap: BacryMuzy2016 derives the continuous Wiener--Hopf relation, while EtesamiZhangSinghalKiyavash2016 Section 4, Equations (13)--(16), works with the full lag-indexed covariance transform; neither states this exact fixed-bin factorization or the image equality for singular acyclic \(A\).
statements.consumer: The image equality supplies the observable state space on which the two-lag recovery theorem is defined.
statements.proof_tex:
Let the law belong to \(\overline{\mathcal M}_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG}}\).  By \(\text{ass:nonnegative-excitation}\), an entry of \(A^d\) is positive only if the support graph contains a directed walk of length \(d\).  If \(d\geq p\), such a walk repeats a vertex and therefore contains a directed cycle.  This contradicts \(\text{ass:acyclic-support}\), under which a self-loop is already a cycle of length one.  Hence
\[
 A^p=0,\qquad \rho(A)=0<\beta,
\tag{1}
\]
where the strict inequality uses \(\text{ass:positive-decay}\).  All remaining membership conditions of \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{stab}}\) are exactly those in \(\text{def:closure-class}\).  Thus the law belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{stab}}\).

Apply \(\text{lem:stable-covariance-semigroup}\).  It gives, with the same definitions of \(B,T,J,Q,K\),
\[
 Q\succ0,\quad C_+(t)=e^{Bt}K,\quad K=A(2\beta I_p-A)Q,
\]
\[
 K-K^{\mathsf T}=AD-DA^{\mathsf T},\quad
 \Gamma_k=T^{k-1}J^2K,\qquad
 \operatorname{im}(\Gamma_1)=\operatorname{im}(K)=\operatorname{im}(A),
\]
and therefore \(\operatorname{rank}(\Gamma_1)=\operatorname{rank}(A)\).  Equation (1) also shows that every eigenvalue of \(B\) equals \(-\beta\); its algebraic multiplicity, Jordan structure, and the rank of \(A\) were never restricted.  Relabeling into topological order permits arbitrary disconnected blocks, while diamonds and proportional rows merely change the entries and rank of the nilpotent matrix.  The displayed conclusions therefore include singular, disconnected, repeated-pole, diamond, and proportional-row cases.

statements.statement: For every law in \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG},+}\), the map \(\Phi_{\Delta,r}\) is well defined and basis invariant, \(r\geq1\), \(F\) represents \(T|_S\), \(q=e^{-\beta\Delta}\), \(E^r=0\), and \(\Phi_{\Delta,r}(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)=(\beta,A,\mu)\). In particular, \((m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\) identifies the labeled graph and every amplitude, decay, and baseline exactly even when \(A\) is singular, disconnected, or has repeated poles.
statements.justification: The theorem isolates a finite sufficient statistic and an explicit inverse for a causal network observed only through coarse counts.
statements.gap: Koyama2025 Section 3.4, page 8, Theorem 2 and Equation (18), proves \(F_{\Delta t}^{(cg)}(\nu\Delta t)=F^{(hw)}(\nu)\Delta t+O(\Delta t^3)\) as \(\Delta t\to0\), and Corollary 1 compares that surrogate spectrum with the binned spectrum; Section 3.5, pages 8--9, Equations (19)--(20), defines a quadratic-form estimator. Kirchner2016 Section 3.2, Theorem 2 and Equation (21), proves \(N^{(\Delta)}\Rightarrow N\) only as \(\Delta\to0\), while Section 3.3, Equations (25)--(28), gives parallel INAR(\(\infty\)) and Hawkes lag equations. EtesamiZhangSinghalKiyavash2016 Corollary 4 and Proposition 6 require full spectral zeros and Laplace transforms, and ZhouPapadogeorgou2025 Theorem 3.1 and Proposition 3.1 use the full aggregated-count law; none gives an exact finite-\(\Delta\) inverse for the original labeled process from one mean and two covariance matrices.
statements.consumer: QiaoCaiWuXiangZhangHao2023's metropolitan cellular-alarm setting can recover within-bin direction at its native one-to-nine-second resolution without imputing latent event times.
statements.proof_tex:
By \(\text{lem:covariance-semigroup}\), nonemptiness gives \(r=\operatorname{rank}(A)\geq1\) and \(S=\operatorname{im}(A)=\operatorname{im}(\Gamma_1)\).  Since \(BA=AB\), the space \(S\) is invariant under \(B\), and therefore under \(T=e^{B\Delta}\) and \(J\).  For an orthonormal basis \(O\) of \(S\), put \(R=O^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_1\).  Then \(\Gamma_1=OR\), and \(R\) has row rank \(r\), so \(RR^{\mathsf T}\) is positive definite and invertible.

There is a unique matrix \(F_0\) satisfying \(TO=OF_0\).  The semigroup identity gives \(\Gamma_2=T\Gamma_1=OF_0R\); multiplication on the left by \(O^{\mathsf T}\) and on the right by the right inverse \(R^{\mathsf T}(RR^{\mathsf T})^{-1}\) yields
\[
 F=O^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_2R^{\mathsf T}(RR^{\mathsf T})^{-1}=F_0.
\]
Thus \(F\) represents \(T|_S\).  If \(A_S=O^{\mathsf T}AO\) denotes the coordinate matrix of \(A|_S\), then \(A_S^r=0\) and
\[
 F=e^{(-\beta I_r+A_S)\Delta}=q_0e^{A_S\Delta},\qquad q_0=e^{-\beta\Delta}\in(0,1).
\]
All eigenvalues of \(e^{A_S\Delta}\) equal one, so \(\operatorname{tr}(F)=rq_0\).  Hence the definition's scalar satisfies \(q=q_0\), and \(\beta^\star=-\Delta^{-1}\log q=\beta\).  Furthermore
\[
 E=q^{-1}F-I_r=e^{A_S\Delta}-I_r
\]
is a polynomial in \(A_S\) with zero constant term.  It is nilpotent and \(E^r=0\).  The mutually inverse exponential and logarithm polynomials on nilpotent matrices give
\[
 \sum_{h=1}^{r-1}\frac{(-1)^{h+1}}hE^h=A_S\Delta,
\]
so \(L^\star=-\beta I_r+A_S\) is exactly the coordinate matrix of \(B|_S\).  Since its only eigenvalue is \(-\beta\), it is invertible.  Since the only eigenvalue of \(F-I_r\) is \(q-1\neq0\), that matrix is also invertible.  On \(S\),
\[
 J_S=(L^\star)^{-1}(F-I_r),\qquad H^\star=L^\star(F-I_r)^{-1}=J_S^{-1},
\]
where commutativity follows because all matrices are polynomials or rational functions of \(A_S\).

The columns of \(K\) lie in \(S\).  Writing \(K=OK_S\), the identity \(\Gamma_1=J^2K\) becomes \(R=J_S^2K_S\).  Therefore
\[
 K^\star=O(H^\star)^2R=OK_S=K.
\]
It follows from \(K-K^{\mathsf T}=AD-DA^{\mathsf T}\) that
\[
 Z_{ij}=A_{ij}\lambda_j-A_{ji}\lambda_i.
\]
Acyclicity forbids a self-loop and forbids the two-cycle consisting of both \(i\to j\) and \(j\to i\).  Nonnegativity and \(\lambda_i>0\) consequently imply, for \(i\neq j\),
\[
 A_{ij}=\frac{\max\{Z_{ij},0\}}{\lambda_j}.
\]
The mean identity gives \(\lambda=m/\Delta\).  Integrating the Hawkes kernel in the stationary mean equation gives \(\lambda=\mu+(A/\beta)\lambda\), and hence \(\mu=(I_p-A/\beta)\lambda\).  Thus every component produced by \(\Phi_{\Delta,r}\) equals the structural component.

Finally, replace \(O\) by another orthonormal basis \(O'=OU\), where \(U\) is orthogonal.  Then \(R'=U^{\mathsf T}R\), \(F'=U^{\mathsf T}FU\), \(E'=U^{\mathsf T}EU\), \(L'=U^{\mathsf T}LU\), and \(H'=U^{\mathsf T}HU\).  Hence \(O'(H')^2R'=OH^2R\).  All later operations are basis free, proving basis invariance.  This argument uses the actual image and actual rank only, so singularity, disconnection, proportional rows, and repeated Jordan poles cause no exception.

statements.statement: Within \(\overline{\mathcal M}_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG}}\), \(\Gamma_1=0\) if and only if \(A=0\). On this stratum \(N_1,\ldots,N_p\) are independent homogeneous Poisson processes with rates \(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_p\), every \(\beta>0\) induces the same observable law, and \(\beta\) is not identified.
statements.justification: The proposition states the exact boundary on which decay recovery must fail and prevents an estimator from fabricating information at the empty graph.
statements.gap: The finite-bin papers treat positive-excitation parameterizations or likelihood identifiability and do not state this complete two-lag observational-equivalence class.
statements.consumer: The proposition tells a graph-recovery pipeline when it must report a set-valued decay rather than a numerical estimate.
statements.proof_tex: The equivalence \(\Gamma_1=0\Longleftrightarrow A=0\) follows immediately from \(\operatorname{rank}(\Gamma_1)=\operatorname{rank}(A)\) in \(\text{lem:covariance-semigroup}\).  If \(A=0\), then \(\text{ass:hawkes-intensity}\) reduces to \(\ell_i(t)=\mu_i\).  For disjoint labeled intervals, the conditional survivor formula obtained by integrating this deterministic hazard is exponential with rate equal to the sum of the corresponding \(\mu_i\)'s, and the conditional label probability at a jump is \(\mu_i/\sum_j\mu_j\).  Iterating these two conditional laws shows that the superposed process is homogeneous Poisson and its labels are independent identically distributed marks with those probabilities.  Poisson thinning therefore gives independent homogeneous Poisson coordinates of rates \(\mu_i\).  The resulting law contains no occurrence of \(\beta\).  Thus every \(\beta>0\), with the same \(\mu\) and \(A=0\), induces the same observable law, so the decay is not identified on precisely this stratum.

statements.statement: For every law in \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG},+}\), \(\Psi_{\Delta,r}(\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)=(\beta,A,\mu)\). Equivalently, after the positive-lag inverse reconstructs \(\widetilde C_{+}(t)=C_{+}(t)\) on \((0,\Delta]\), the formula \(D=\Delta^{-1}[\Gamma_0-\int_0^\Delta(\Delta-t)\{C_{+}(t)+C_{+}(t)^{\mathsf T}\}\,dt]\) recovers \(\lambda=\operatorname{diag}(D)\), so the mean is redundant.
statements.justification: The result determines whether the diagonal jump in zero-lag bin covariance carries all missing first-order information.
statements.gap: Hawkes1971Spectra and BacryMuzy2016 keep intensity as a separate first-order input, while AchabBacryGaiffasMastromatteoMuzy2017 adds third-order cumulants rather than isolating intensity from \(\Gamma_0\).
statements.consumer: Legacy alarm archives that retain covariance summaries but not reliable marginal count totals can still identify the directed Hawkes mechanism.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG},+}\), the bin-count sequence \(X\) is strongly mixing at a geometric rate. Fix \(p\), \(\Delta\), and \(\kappa\in(0,1/2)\). Uniformly over \(P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)\), the Poisson immigration--birth representation has genealogical depth at most \(p-1\): every child follows a directed edge of \(G(A)\), so a longer lineage would repeat a label and create a directed cycle. Conditional offspring delays have density \(\beta e^{-\beta u}\), \(\beta\geq\underline\beta=-\Delta^{-1}\log(1-\kappa)\), every event has total offspring mean at most \(\overline\nu=\overline a/\underline\beta\), and the total immigrant rate is at most \(\overline\mu\). Consequently the cluster duration has the uniform tail bound \(P_{\theta}(D_{\mathrm{cl}}>u)\leq C_{\mathrm{mix}}e^{-c_{\mathrm{mix}}u}\), where \(c_{\mathrm{mix}}=\underline\beta/2\) and \(C_{\mathrm{mix}}=1+\{1+2\overline\mu c_{\mathrm{mix}}^{-1}e^{c_{\mathrm{mix}}\Delta}\}\sum_{d=1}^{p-1}(2\overline a/\underline\beta)^d\). Coupling the restrictions of the immigrant Poisson measure on the two sides of a bin gap then gives \(\alpha_{X,\theta}(h)\leq C_{\mathrm{mix}}e^{-c_{\mathrm{mix}}h\Delta}\) for every integer \(h\geq1\), and \(\alpha_{Y,\theta}(h)\leq C_{\mathrm{mix}}e^{-c_{\mathrm{mix}}(h-2)_{+}\Delta}\) for every integer \(h\geq1\).
statements.justification: This lemma turns feed-forward structure and bounded primitive parameters into the uniform dependence rate required by the HAC argument.
statements.gap: BolyCheyssonNguyen2024 provides compatible general multivariate Hawkes mixing background but does not state this geometric rate from finite genealogical depth; the rate and constants here come from the acyclic common-exponential cluster construction.
statements.consumer: The raw-moment central limit theorem can invoke a derived uniform geometric rate instead of assuming one as a separate model restriction.
statements.proof_tex:
Acyclicity implies that a genealogical line uses at most \(p-1\) edges: each child follows an edge of \(G(A)\), and a line of length at least \(p\) repeats a label and contains a directed cycle.  For a parent of label \(j\), the total number of children is Poisson with mean \(\sum_iA_{ij}/\beta\).  The parameter envelope and the column norm inequality give
\[
 \sum_iA_{ij}\leq\sqrt p\|Ae_j\|_2\leq\sqrt p\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\overline a,
\]
while the decay margin gives \(\beta\geq\underline\beta\).  Thus every total offspring mean is at most \(\overline\nu=\overline a/\underline\beta\).  Conditional on a child occurring, its delay has density \(\beta e^{-\beta u}\).  Also \(\sum_i\mu_i\leq\sqrt p\|\mu\|_2\leq\overline\mu\).

Let \(c=c_{\mathrm{mix}}=\underline\beta/2\).  A descendant at generation \(d\) has a path delay equal in law, conditional on its path, to a sum \(S_d\) of \(d\) independent exponential variables of rate \(\beta\).  Exponential Markov inequality gives
\[
 P(S_d>u)\leq e^{-cu}\left(\frac{\beta}{\beta-c}\right)^d\leq2^de^{-cu}.
\]
The expected number of generation-\(d\) descendants is at most \(\overline\nu^d\).  A union bound through expected descendant counts therefore yields
\[
 P(D_{\mathrm{cl}}>u)\leq e^{-cu}\sum_{d=1}^{p-1}(2\overline\nu)^d
 \leq C_{\mathrm{mix}}e^{-cu}.
\]

For the strong-mixing bound, couple the past bins and future bins by using independent copies of every immigrant cluster that intersects both sides of the gap.  If the past ends at time \(\Delta\) and the future begins at \(h\Delta\), such a cluster must have immigrant time \(s\leq\Delta\) and duration exceeding \(h\Delta-s\).  The Poisson union bound and the preceding sharper tail with constant \(C_0=\sum_{d=1}^{p-1}(2\overline a/\underline\beta)^d\) give
\[
 P(\text{a crossing cluster})
 \leq\overline\mu\int_{-\infty}^{\Delta}C_0e^{-c(h\Delta-s)}ds
 =\overline\mu c^{-1}e^{c\Delta}C_0e^{-ch\Delta}
 \leq C_{\mathrm{mix}}e^{-ch\Delta}.
\]
On the complement, the two sigma-fields are functions of disjoint restrictions of the immigrant Poisson measure and independent offspring marks.  The coupling inequality thus proves \(\alpha_{X,\theta}(h)\leq C_{\mathrm{mix}}e^{-c_{\mathrm{mix}}h\Delta}\).  The process \(Y_k\) depends only on \(X_k,X_{k+1},X_{k+2}\), so its two sigma-fields have an \(X\)-bin gap of \((h-2)_+\), yielding the stated bound for \(\alpha_{Y,\theta}(h)\).  With parameters fixed, the same calculation uses finite law-specific constants and proves geometric mixing on the whole nonempty class.

statements.statement: Every fixed law in \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG},+}\) has finite bin-count moments of every order. Fix \(p\), \(\Delta\), and \(\kappa\in(0,1/2)\). Uniformly over \(P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)\), the total progeny of any immigrant cluster is dominated by a depth-\(p-1\) Poisson branching tree whose moment-generating functions obey \(g_0(z)=e^z\) and \(g_d(z)=\exp[z+\overline\nu\{g_{d-1}(z)-1\}]\). For every integer \(u\in\{1,\ldots,8\}\), differentiating the stationary Poisson-cluster generating functional and using the duration bound in \(\text{lem:finite-depth-geometric-mixing}\) gives \[\operatorname{cum}_u(\lVert X_0\rVert_1)\leq\overline\mu\left[\Delta g_{p-1}^{(u)}(0)+2c_{\mathrm{mix}}^{-1}\{C_{\mathrm{mix}}g_{p-1}^{(2u)}(0)\}^{1/2}\right].\] The complete moment--cumulant formula therefore yields the named finite constant \(M_8=M_8(p,\Delta,\kappa)\) and \(\sup_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}\mathbb E_{\theta}\lVert X_0\rVert_2^8\leq M_8\).
statements.justification: The recursive cluster bound supplies the fourth moments of the quadratic raw-moment process needed for uniform long-run covariance estimation.
statements.gap: CheyssonLang2022 assumes moment regularity for its spectral limit theory; it does not derive a uniform eighth-bin-count envelope from bounded acyclic Hawkes primitives.
statements.consumer: Uniform HAC consistency and Gaussian calibration no longer depend on an unexplained independent moment assumption.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(T_d\) be total progeny when at most \(d\) generations remain.  The offspring-count domination in \(\text{lem:finite-depth-geometric-mixing}\) gives \(T_0=1\) and the stochastic recursion
\[
 T_d\preceq1+\sum_{a=1}^{P_{\overline\nu}}T_{d-1,a},
\]
where \(P_{\overline\nu}\) is Poisson with mean \(\overline\nu\) and the variables on the right are independent.  Taking moment-generating functions proves inductively
\[
 E(e^{zT_d})\leq g_d(z),\quad g_0(z)=e^z,\quad
 g_d(z)=\exp[z+\overline\nu\{g_{d-1}(z)-1\}].
\]
Every \(g_d\) is finite in a neighborhood of zero, so \(E(T_d^u)\leq g_d^{(u)}(0)\) for every fixed \(u\).

For an immigrant at time \(s\), let \(Z_s\) be its cluster's number of points in \([0,\Delta]\).  The Poisson-cluster generating functional implies, by differentiating at zero, that the \(u\)-th cumulant of \(\|X_0\|_1\) is the immigrant-rate integral of \(E(Z_s^u)\).  This identity is also obtained directly by partitioning immigrant time into bounded intervals, using additivity of cumulants for independent compound-Poisson sums, and applying monotone convergence.  Immigrants after \(\Delta\) contribute zero.  For \(0\leq s\leq\Delta\), \(Z_s\leq T_{p-1}\).  For \(s<0\), the event \(Z_s>0\) implies \(D_{\mathrm{cl}}>-s\), and Cauchy--Schwarz with the duration bound gives
\[
 E(Z_s^u)\leq\{E(T_{p-1}^{2u})P(D_{\mathrm{cl}}>-s)\}^{1/2}
 \leq\{g_{p-1}^{(2u)}(0)C_{\mathrm{mix}}\}^{1/2}e^{c_{\mathrm{mix}}s/2}.
\]
Since the total immigrant rate is at most \(\overline\mu\), integration over \(( -\infty,0)\) and \([0,\Delta]\) yields, for \(1\leq u\leq8\),
\[
 \operatorname{cum}_u(\|X_0\|_1)\leq\overline\mu\left[\Delta g_{p-1}^{(u)}(0)+2c_{\mathrm{mix}}^{-1}
 \{C_{\mathrm{mix}}g_{p-1}^{(2u)}(0)\}^{1/2}\right].
\]
The eighth moment is the complete Bell polynomial in the first eight cumulants.  Substituting these eight explicit upper bounds defines a finite \(M_8(p,\Delta,\kappa)\).  Finally \(\|X_0\|_2\leq\|X_0\|_1\), proving the asserted uniform eighth-moment bound.  With parameters fixed, the same finite-depth recursion has finite constants of every order, proving all fixed-law moments.

statements.statement: For every fixed law in \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG},+}\), \(\widehat\xi_n\to\xi\) and \(\widehat\eta_n=\mathcal C(\widehat\xi_n)\to\eta=(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\) in probability. Fix \(p\), \(\Delta\), and \(\kappa\in(0,1/2)\). The derived geometric-mixing and eighth-moment bounds imply that \(\Omega(\theta)\) is finite uniformly over \(P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)\) and \[\sup_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}d_{\mathrm{BL}}\left(\mathcal L_{\theta}\{\sqrt n(\widehat\xi_n-\xi(\theta))\},\mathcal N\{0,\Omega(\theta)\}\right)\longrightarrow0.\] Because \(\widehat\eta_n=\mathcal C(\widehat\xi_n)\) and \(\eta=\mathcal C(\xi)=(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\), the same uniform statement holds for \(\sqrt n(\widehat\eta_n-\eta(\theta))\) with covariance \(D\mathcal C_{\xi(\theta)}\Omega(\theta)D\mathcal C_{\xi(\theta)}^{\mathsf T}\). If \(b_n\to\infty\) and \(b_n=o(n^{1/2})\), then for every \(\varepsilon>0\), \[\sup_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}P_{\theta}\{\lVert\widehat\Omega_n-\Omega(\theta)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}>\varepsilon\}\longrightarrow0.\]
statements.justification: A joint dependent-data limit for precisely the moments entering the inverse is required before any graph-wide uncertainty statement is credible.
statements.gap: CheyssonLang2022 proves fixed-bin Whittle asymptotics, while BolyCheyssonNguyen2024 supplies general mixing background; neither derives the finite-depth uniform envelopes or the joint raw-lag-moment Gaussian and HAC limits in the coordinates of this inverse.
statements.consumer: The rank-adaptive inverse and simultaneous graph confidence set use this Gaussian moment experiment.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(N_n=n-2\) and \(U_k=Y_k-\xi\).  We first derive the moment and covariance bounds used below.  By \(\text{lem:uniform-bin-eighth-moment}\), uniformly on \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)\),
\[
 \mathbb E_\theta\lVert Y_0\rVert_2^4\leq C_Y<\infty,
\tag{1}
\]
because each quadratic coordinate of \(Y_0\) is bounded in absolute value by a constant depending only on \(p\) times \(\sum_{a=0}^2\lVert X_a\rVert_2^2\), and stationarity gives the same eighth-moment bound for every \(X_a\).  The fixed-law version of (1) follows from the first sentence of that lemma.  For centered scalar coordinates \(U=Y_{0,a}-\mathbb EY_{0,a}\) and \(V=Y_{h,b}-\mathbb EY_{h,b}\), clip at level \(M\geq1\).  The definition of strong mixing, followed by adding and subtracting the clipped variables and applying Cauchy--Schwarz and Markov inequalities, gives
\[
 |\operatorname{Cov}(U,V)|
 \leq4M^2\alpha_Y(h)+C M^{-1}.
\tag{2}
\]
Taking \(M=\max\{1,\alpha_Y(h)^{-1/6}\}\), with the zero-mixing case obtained by first fixing \(M\) and then sending \(M\) to infinity, yields
\[
 |\operatorname{Cov}(U,V)|\leq C'\alpha_Y(h)^{1/6}.
\tag{3}
\]
The exponential envelope in \(\text{lem:finite-depth-geometric-mixing}\) makes the right side summable uniformly.  Since the dimension \(d_0=p+2p^2\) is fixed,
\[
 \sup_{\theta:P_\theta\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}
 \sum_{h\in\mathbb Z}\lVert\operatorname{Cov}_\theta(Y_0,Y_h)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}<\infty.
\tag{4}
\]
This proves both that \(\Omega(\theta)\) is well defined and uniformly bounded and that
\[
 \sup_\theta\mathbb E_\theta
 \left\lVert N_n^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{N_n-1}U_k\right\rVert_2^2
 \leq C N_n^{-1}.
\tag{5}
\]
Consequently \(\widehat\xi_n\to\xi\) in probability, pointwise and uniformly on the margin class.  The map \(\mathcal C\) in \(\text{def:centering-map}\) is a quadratic polynomial, so it is continuous; hence \(\widehat\eta_n=\mathcal C(\widehat\xi_n)\to\mathcal C(\xi)=\eta=(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\).  This proves the two asserted probability limits, including for a fixed law outside the margin class by using the law-dependent versions of (1)--(5).

We shall also need a higher derived moment, not a new hypothesis.  The finite recursion displayed in \(\text{lem:uniform-bin-eighth-moment}\) is finite in a neighborhood of zero at every depth at most \(p-1\).  Repeating that lemma's Poisson-cluster cumulant calculation through order sixteen, using \(g_{p-1}^{(32)}(0)<\infty\) in its Cauchy--Schwarz duration-tail step, gives
\[
 \sup_{\theta:P_\theta\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}
 \mathbb E_\theta\lVert X_0\rVert_2^{16}<\infty,
 \qquad
 \sup_\theta\mathbb E_\theta\lVert Y_0\rVert_2^8<\infty.
\tag{6}
\]
Only the same bounded depth, offspring envelope, immigrant envelope, and exponential cluster-duration bound are used.

We next prove the uniform Gaussian assertion rather than importing a mixing central limit theorem.  Fix a unit vector \(a\in\mathbb R^{d_0}\).  Divide \(0,\ldots,N_n-1\) into large blocks of length \(\ell_n=\lfloor N_n^{1/2}\rfloor\), gaps of length \(g_n=\lceil c_0\log N_n\rceil\), and a terminal remainder, where \(c_0>(2c_{\mathrm{mix}}\Delta)^{-1}\).  There are \(v_n\leq N_n/\ell_n\) large blocks.  By (4), the discarded gaps and remainder have variance at most \(C(v_ng_n+\ell_n)=o(N_n)\).  Telescoping the product of the bounded large-block characteristic functions and applying the bounded strong-mixing covariance inequality at each gap changes that product to the corresponding product for independent block copies by at most
\[
 v_n\alpha_Y(g_n-2)\leq C N_n^{1/2}e^{-c_{\mathrm{mix}}\Delta g_n}=o(1)
\tag{7}
\]
uniformly in \(\theta\).  This uses only strong mixing; no absolute-regularity coupling is invoked.

Expanding a fourth power and ordering its four time indices, repeated clipping applied to the two groups separated by the largest adjacent gap, with the eighth moment in (6), gives a positive power of the geometric mixing coefficient.  Summing that envelope and bounding coincident indices by (6) yields, uniformly for every interval \(I\) of length \(\ell\),
\[
 \mathbb E_\theta\left|\sum_{k\in I}a^{\mathsf T}U_k\right|^4\leq C_1\ell^2.
\tag{8}
\]
If \(B_{b,n}\) are the independent copies of the large-block sums, then
\[
 N_n^{-2}\sum_{b=1}^{v_n}\mathbb E_\theta|B_{b,n}|^4
 \leq C_1v_n\ell_n^2N_n^{-2}
 =O(\ell_n/N_n)=o(1).
\tag{9}
\]
Taylor expansion of each independent-block characteristic function through second order, with (9) controlling the summed remainder, shows that the characteristic function of \(N_n^{-1/2}\sum_bB_{b,n}\) differs uniformly from that of a centered normal variable with the same variance by \(o(1)\).  By (4), that variance differs from \(a^{\mathsf T}\Omega(\theta)a\) by the covariance tail and by \(O(g_n/\ell_n+\ell_n/N_n)=o(1)\).  Equations (7)--(9) and the negligible gaps therefore give the scalar Gaussian approximation for every \(a\), uniformly in \(\theta\).

To pass to vectors without a hidden uniformity assumption, suppose the displayed bounded-Lipschitz conclusion failed.  There would be a sequence \(\theta_n\) and a positive lower bound on its discrepancy.  The uniformly bounded matrices \(\Omega(\theta_n)\) have a convergent subsequence.  Along a further subsequence, the preceding scalar characteristic-function calculation applied to each vector in a countable dense subset of the unit sphere, together with the uniform second-moment bound (5), gives convergence of the vector characteristic functions to those of the centered normal law with the limiting covariance.  Fourier approximation of bounded Lipschitz functions on a large ball, and (5) outside that ball, then gives bounded-Lipschitz convergence, a contradiction.  Thus
\[
 \sup_{\theta:P_\theta\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}
 d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(
 \mathcal L_\theta\{\sqrt n(\widehat\xi_n-\xi(\theta))\},
 \mathcal N\{0,\Omega(\theta)\}\right)\longrightarrow0,
\tag{10}
\]
where replacing \(N_n\) by \(n\) is harmless because \(N_n/n\to1\).

The derivative of \(\mathcal C\) is uniformly bounded on the moment set supplied by (1), and its exact quadratic expansion has remainder bounded by \(C\lVert\widehat\xi_n-\xi\rVert_2^2\).  Equations (5) and (10) therefore give, uniformly,
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\eta_n-\eta(\theta)\}
 =D\mathcal C_{\xi(\theta)}\sqrt n\{\widehat\xi_n-\xi(\theta)\}+o_{P_\theta}(1),
\tag{11}
\]
which proves the asserted centered-moment Gaussian approximation with covariance \(D\mathcal C_{\xi(\theta)}\Omega(\theta)D\mathcal C_{\xi(\theta)}^{\mathsf T}\).

It remains to prove the Bartlett heteroskedasticity-and-autocorrelation assertion.  Let
\[
 \widetilde\Xi_h=N_n^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{N_n-h-1}U_kU_{k+h}^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Repeated clipping as in (2), now for products of at most four coordinates and using (6), bounds each joint fourth cumulant by a constant times a positive power of the mixing coefficient across the largest separating gap.  After ordering the four time arguments, the geometric mixing envelope makes these cumulants absolutely summable, uniformly in every free translation and in the remaining lag indices.  Expanding a covariance of two products gives explicitly
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(U_0^aU_h^b,U_t^cU_{t+h'}^d)
 =\operatorname{cum}(U_0^a,U_h^b,U_t^c,U_{t+h'}^d)
 +\operatorname{Cov}(U_0^a,U_t^c)\operatorname{Cov}(U_h^b,U_{t+h'}^d)
 +\operatorname{Cov}(U_0^a,U_{t+h'}^d)\operatorname{Cov}(U_h^b,U_t^c).
\tag{12}
\]
The cumulant sum and both convolution sums in (12) are bounded uniformly by (3), (6), and the preceding largest-gap bound.  Consequently, for all \(0\leq h,h'\leq b_n\),
\[
 \left|\operatorname{Cov}\{(\widetilde\Xi_h)_{ab},(\widetilde\Xi_{h'})_{cd}\}\right|
 \leq C_2N_n^{-1}.
\tag{13}
\]
Summing (13) over the finitely many coordinates and the \((b_n+1)^2\) lag pairs yields
\[
 \mathbb E_\theta\left\lVert
 \sum_{h=0}^{b_n}w(h/b_n)
 \{\widetilde\Xi_h-\mathbb E_\theta\widetilde\Xi_h\}
 \right\rVert_{\mathrm F}^2
 \leq C_3b_n^2/N_n=o(1).
\tag{14}
\]
For the expectation, \(\mathbb E\widetilde\Xi_h=(1-h/N_n)\operatorname{Cov}(Y_0,Y_h)\).  Since \(w(0)=1\), \(w(h/b_n)\to1\) for fixed \(h\), and (4) supplies a uniform summable envelope, splitting at a fixed lag and then sending that lag to infinity proves that the expectation of the symmetrized lag-window sum converges uniformly to \(\Omega(\theta)\).

Finally, expanding \((Y_k-\overline Y_n)(Y_{k+h}-\overline Y_n)^{\mathsf T}\) around \(U_kU_{k+h}^{\mathsf T}\), using (5) and the boundary pieces of length at most \(h\), shows that replacing \(\xi\) by \(\overline Y_n\) changes the complete lag-window sum by
\[
 O_{P_\theta}\!\left(b_n\lVert\overline Y_n-\xi\rVert_2
 +b_n\lVert\overline Y_n-\xi\rVert_2^2\right)=o_{P_\theta}(1)
\tag{15}
\]
uniformly, because \(b_n=o(n^{1/2})\).  The empty-sum convention in \(\text{def:hac-estimator}\) makes this expansion valid for every finite sample.  Combining (4), (14), and (15), and using \(\lVert M\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\lVert M\rVert_{\mathrm F}\), proves the stated uniform operator-norm consistency of \(\widehat\Omega_n\).

statements.statement: For every fixed law in \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG},+}\), if \(t_n\downarrow0\), \(\sqrt n\,t_n\to\infty\), \(a_n\downarrow0\), and \(\sqrt n\,a_n\to\infty\), then \(\mathbb P(\widehat r_n=r)\to1\), \(\widehat\theta_n\to(\beta,A,\mu)\) in probability, and \(\mathbb P(\widehat G_n=G(A))\to1\). Fix \(p\), \(\Delta\), and \(\kappa\in(0,1/2)\). On \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)\), under the long-run-covariance nonsingularity and bandwidth conditions, rank selection is uniformly consistent and the structural estimator is uniformly root-\(n\) tight: \[\sup_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}P_{\theta}(\widehat r_n\neq r(\theta))\longrightarrow0,\] \[\lim_{M\to\infty}\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}P_{\theta}\!\left[\sqrt n\{ |\widehat\beta_n-\beta|+\lVert\widehat A_n-A\rVert_{\mathrm F}+\lVert\widehat\mu_n-\mu\rVert_2\}>M\right]=0.\] For every \(\varepsilon>0\), \[\sup_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}P_{\theta}\{\lVert\widehat\Omega_n-\Omega(\theta)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}>\varepsilon\}\longrightarrow0.\]
statements.justification: The theorem converts exact identification into a rank-adaptive estimator while making every conditioning margin explicit.

statements.proof_tex:
We separate the fixed-law and uniform arguments.  Under a fixed law in \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG},+}\), the fixed-law moment and geometric-mixing conclusions of \(\text{lem:uniform-bin-eighth-moment}\) and \(\text{lem:finite-depth-geometric-mixing}\), together with the clipping calculation (2)--(3) in \(\text{lem:bin-moment-limit}\), imply
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat\xi_n-\xi)=O_P(1),
 \qquad
 \sqrt n(\widehat\eta_n-\eta)=O_P(1),
\tag{1}
\]
the second relation following from the quadratic centering map in \(\text{def:centering-map}\).

Let \(r=\operatorname{rank}(\Gamma_1)\).  By \(\text{thm:two-lag-exact-recovery}\) and \(A\neq0\) in \(\text{def:model-class}\), \(r\geq1\).  The singular-value min--max formula and the triangle inequality give, for every \(s\),
\[
 |\sigma_s(\widehat\Gamma_{1,n})-\sigma_s(\Gamma_1)|
 \leq\lVert\widehat\Gamma_{1,n}-\Gamma_1\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.
\tag{2}
\]
At a fixed law \(\sigma_r(\Gamma_1)>0\), while \(\sigma_s(\Gamma_1)=0\) for \(s>r\).  Thus (1)--(2), \(t_n\downarrow0\), and \(\sqrt n\,t_n\to\infty\) imply
\[
 P(\widehat r_n=r)\longrightarrow1.
\tag{3}
\]

We next establish the required local regularity without choosing singular-vector signs.  Put \(M_1=\Gamma_1\Gamma_1^{\mathsf T}\).  Choose a closed contour \(\mathfrak c\) separating its \(r\) positive eigenvalues from zero.  Diagonalization of the real symmetric matrix \(M_1\) verifies that the active projector equals
\[
 P_S=\frac{1}{2\pi\mathrm i}\int_{\mathfrak c}(zI_p-M_1)^{-1}\,dz.
\tag{4}
\]
For a perturbation \(H\), the algebraic resolvent identity
\[
 (zI_p-M_1-H)^{-1}-(zI_p-M_1)^{-1}
 =(zI_p-M_1-H)^{-1}H(zI_p-M_1)^{-1}
\tag{5}
\]
shows first local Lipschitz continuity and, after one further substitution, a quadratic remainder after the linear term.  Hence the rank-\(r\) spectral projector is Fr\'{e}chet differentiable.  If \(O_0\) is any fixed orthonormal frame of \(S\), then
\[
 O(P)=PO_0\{O_0^{\mathsf T}PO_0\}^{-1/2}
\tag{6}
\]
is a differentiable orthonormal frame for every projector \(P\) close enough to \(P_S\).

If a frame is replaced by \(OU\) for an orthogonal \(U\), the quantities in \(\text{def:two-lag-inverse}\) transform as
\[
 R\mapsto U^{\mathsf T}R,\quad F\mapsto U^{\mathsf T}FU,\quad
 E\mapsto U^{\mathsf T}EU,\quad L^\star\mapsto U^{\mathsf T}L^\star U,\quad
 H^\star\mapsto U^{\mathsf T}H^\star U.
\tag{7}
\]
Therefore \(O(H^\star)^2R\), its skew part, \(A^\star\), and \(\mu^\star\) do not change.  Thus (6) may be used to differentiate the actual basis-invariant empirical inverse even if the measurable singular-value-decomposition rule in \(\text{def:rank-adaptive-estimator}\) chooses another frame.

At the population point every denominator is interior.  Indeed, \(RR^{\mathsf T}\succ0\), \(q=e^{-\beta\Delta}\in(0,1)\), and every eigenvalue of \(F\) is \(q\), so \(F-I_r\) is invertible.  Positive baselines imply \(\lambda_j=m_j/\Delta>0\).  Acyclicity gives \(A^p=0\), and hence
\[
 (I_p-A/\beta)^{-1}=\sum_{d=0}^{p-1}(A/\beta)^d.
\tag{8}
\]
Equations (4)--(8), continuity of matrix inversion, smoothness of \(-\Delta^{-1}\log q\) on \((0,1)\), and the finite polynomial defining \(L^\star\) show that the inverse before positive parts is locally Lipschitz.  The scalar map \(x\mapsto\max\{x,0\}\) is globally one-Lipschitz, so the entire recovery map is locally Lipschitz.  All strict conditions defining \(\mathcal V_n\) hold at the population point and persist in a neighborhood.  Equations (1) and (3), followed by \(\text{thm:two-lag-exact-recovery}\), therefore yield
\[
 \widehat\theta_n\longrightarrow(\beta,A,\mu),
 \qquad
 \sqrt n\lVert\widehat A_n-A\rVert_{\mathrm F}=O_P(1),
 \qquad
 P(\mathcal V_n^c)\longrightarrow0.
\tag{9}
\]
The sentinel is used only on the last event and hence does not affect these limits.

Let \(a_{\min}=\min\{A_{ij}:A_{ij}>0\}>0\); this minimum exists because \(p\) is finite and \(A\neq0\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(a_n<a_{\min}/2\).  On
\[
 \lVert\widehat A_n-A\rVert_{\max}<\min\{a_n,a_{\min}/2\},
\tag{10}
\]
no absent edge is selected and no present edge is deleted.  By (9) and the stated condition \(\sqrt n\,a_n\to\infty\), the probability of the complement of (10) tends to zero.  This proves all fixed-law assertions.

Now fix \(p\), \(\Delta\), and \(\kappa\).  By \(\text{lem:bin-moment-limit}\), \(\sqrt n(\widehat\xi_n-\xi(\theta))\) is uniformly tight.  The uniform moment bound controls \(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2\), so the derivative of the centering map is uniformly bounded and
\[
 \sqrt n\lVert\widehat\eta_n-\eta(\theta)\rVert=O_{P_\theta}(1)
 \quad\text{uniformly in }\theta.
\tag{11}
\]
By \(\text{ass:rank-gap}\), every positive singular value is at least \(\kappa\).  Combining (2), (11), \(t_n\to0\), and \(\sqrt n\,t_n\to\infty\) gives
\[
 \sup_{\theta:P_\theta\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}
 P_\theta\{\widehat r_n\neq r(\theta)\}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{12}
\]

We expose all remaining uniform conditioning margins.  First,
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(RR^{\mathsf T})=\sigma_r(\Gamma_1)^2\geq\kappa^2.
\tag{13}
\]
Second, \(\text{ass:decay-margin}\) gives \(q\in[\kappa,1-\kappa]\).  The moment bound and (13) bound \(\lVert F\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\).  Since every eigenvalue of \(F\) is \(q\), including for repeated poles and singular excitation matrices,
\[
 |\det(F-I_r)|=(1-q)^r\geq\kappa^r.
\tag{14}
\]
For any \(r\times r\) matrix \(M\), the product of its singular values equals \(|\det M|\), so
\[
 \sigma_{\min}(M)\geq |\det M|\lVert M\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^{-(r-1)}.
\tag{15}
\]
Equations (14)--(15) uniformly bound \((F-I_r)^{-1}\).  The finite logarithm has degree at most \(p-1\), and its derivative is uniformly bounded because both \(q^{-1}\) and \(F\) are bounded.  Assumption \(\text{ass:intensity-gap}\) gives \(\lambda_j\geq\kappa\) in every edge division.  Finally, \(\beta\geq\underline\beta=-\Delta^{-1}\log(1-\kappa)>0\), and \(\text{ass:parameter-envelope}\) with (8) gives
\[
 \lVert(I_p-A/\beta)^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq\sum_{d=0}^{p-1}(\kappa^{-1}/\underline\beta)^d.
\tag{16}
\]
Thus every strict validity condition persists on a neighborhood of a common radius, while (4)--(6) have a common derivative bound because the positive and zero spectra are separated by \(\kappa^2\).  Taking the maximum over the finitely many ranks \(1,\ldots,p\) gives a common local Lipschitz constant for the basis-invariant inverse.

Combining this common Lipschitz bound with (11)--(12) proves
\[
 \lim_{M\to\infty}\limsup_{n\to\infty}
 \sup_{\theta:P_\theta\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}
 P_\theta\!\left[
 \sqrt n\{ |\widehat\beta_n-\beta|+
 \lVert\widehat A_n-A\rVert_{\mathrm F}+
 \lVert\widehat\mu_n-\mu\rVert_2\}>M\right]=0.
\tag{17}
\]
The exceptional sentinel contribution is bounded by the probability in (12) plus the probability that (11) leaves the common validity neighborhood, both uniformly negligible.  The final assertion about \(\widehat\Omega_n\) is exactly the Bartlett-HAC conclusion of \(\text{lem:bin-moment-limit}\) under \(\text{ass:hac-bandwidth}\).  No Gaussian law for the nonsmooth positive-part amplitude map has been used.

statements.statement: Fix \(p\), \(\Delta\), and \(\kappa\in(0,1/2)\). If \(t_n,a_n\downarrow0\), \(\sqrt n\,t_n\to\infty\), and \(\sqrt n\,a_n\to\infty\), then the separately thresholded graph \(\widehat G_n=\{j\to i:\widehat A_{ij}>a_n\}\) satisfies \[\sup_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}P_{\theta}\{\widehat G_n\neq G(A)\}\longrightarrow0.\]
statements.justification: Vanishing thresholds separate model selection from fixed-level confidence inversion and eliminate persistent false inclusions at null coordinates.
statements.gap: Fixed-level simultaneous intervals control graph inclusion but cannot make null-coordinate selection errors vanish; existing exact-event-time Hawkes selectors do not establish this uniform fixed-bin inverse result.
statements.consumer: Cellular-alarm analysts obtain a support-consistent point graph separately from the conservative graph confidence set.
statements.proof_tex:
By \(\text{thm:rank-adaptive-estimation}\),
\[
 \sqrt n\lVert\widehat A_n-A\rVert_{\max}=O_{P_\theta}(1)
\tag{1}
\]
uniformly on \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)\), since the maximum norm is bounded by the Frobenius norm.  We convert \(\text{ass:edge-gap}\), which is stated for the signed jump, to a uniform amplitude margin.  Acyclicity gives \(A^p=0\) and therefore
\[
 \lambda=(I_p-A/\beta)^{-1}\mu
 =\sum_{d=0}^{p-1}(A/\beta)^d\mu.
\tag{2}
\]
On the margin class, \(\beta\geq\underline\beta=-\Delta^{-1}\log(1-\kappa)\), \(\lVert A\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\kappa^{-1}\), and \(\lVert\mu\rVert_2\leq\kappa^{-1}\).  Hence
\[
 \max_j\lambda_j\leq\lVert\lambda\rVert_2
 \leq\Lambda_\kappa:=\kappa^{-1}
 \sum_{d=0}^{p-1}(\kappa^{-1}/\underline\beta)^d<\infty.
\tag{3}
\]
For a true edge \(j\to i\), acyclicity excludes \(i\to j\), and the skew-jump identity in \(\text{thm:two-lag-exact-recovery}\) gives \(Z_{ij}=A_{ij}\lambda_j\).  Thus \(\text{ass:edge-gap}\) and (3) imply
\[
 A_{ij}=|Z_{ij}|/\lambda_j\geq\kappa/\Lambda_\kappa.
\tag{4}
\]
For an absent directed edge, \(A_{ij}=0\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(a_n<\kappa/(2\Lambda_\kappa)\).  On the event
\[
 \lVert\widehat A_n-A\rVert_{\max}
 <\min\{a_n,\kappa/(2\Lambda_\kappa)\},
\tag{5}
\]
there are neither false inclusions nor false exclusions, so \(\widehat G_n=G(A)\).  By (1) and the stated condition \(\sqrt n\,a_n\to\infty\), the probability of the complement of (5) tends to zero uniformly.  This proves the proposition.

statements.statement: For fixed \(p\), \(\Delta\), and \(\kappa\in(0,1/2)\), the composite \(\zeta\circ\Phi_{\Delta,r(\theta)}\circ\mathcal C\), evaluated through the signed jump before the positive-part edge map, is Fr\'{e}chet differentiable at \(\xi(\theta)\). Let \[W(\theta)=D(\zeta\circ\Phi_{\Delta,r(\theta)}\circ\mathcal C)_{\xi(\theta)}\,\Omega(\theta)\,D(\zeta\circ\Phi_{\Delta,r(\theta)}\circ\mathcal C)_{\xi(\theta)}^{\mathsf T}.\] Under the derived geometric-mixing and eighth-moment lemmas and the long-run-covariance nonsingularity and bandwidth conditions of \(\text{thm:rank-adaptive-estimation}\), \[\sup_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}d_{\mathrm{BL}}\left(\mathcal L_{\theta}\left[\sqrt n\left\{\zeta(\widehat\theta_n)-\zeta(\theta)\right\}\right],\mathcal N\{0,W(\theta)\}\right)\longrightarrow0,\] and the direct composite estimator \(\widehat W_n\) in the corrected \(\text{def:hac-estimator}\) is uniformly consistent for \(W(\theta)\). Gaussian-maximum calibration with \(\widehat W_n\) yields \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}P_{\theta}\left\{\zeta_{ij}(\theta)\in I_{ij,n}\text{ for every }1\leq i<j\leq p\right\}\geq1-\alpha,\] and consequently \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}P_{\theta}\{G(A)\in\mathcal C_n(1-\alpha)\}\geq1-\alpha.\]
statements.justification: Conservative simultaneous sign inversion makes uncertainty about every directed edge visible without treating fixed-level exclusions as a support-consistent selector.

statements.proof_tex:
Let \(d=p(p-1)/2\), and let \(g_r\) map the raw moment vector to the \(d\) upper-triangular entries of the recovered signed jump \(Z^\star=K^\star-(K^\star)^{\mathsf T}\), using the rank-\(r\) image construction.  On \(\mathcal V_n\), the definitions give, for every \(i<j\),
\[
 \lambda_j^\star A_{ij}^\star-\lambda_i^\star A_{ji}^\star
 =\max\{Z_{ij}^\star,0\}-\max\{-Z_{ij}^\star,0\}
 =Z_{ij}^\star.
\tag{1}
\]
Moreover, \(\mu^\star=(I_p-A^\star/\beta^\star)\lambda^\star\), and invertibility of \(I_p-A^\star/\beta^\star\) is part of \(\mathcal V_n\); hence the intensity computed inside \(\zeta(\widehat\theta_n)\) is exactly \(\lambda^\star\).  On \(\mathcal V_n^c\), both \(\widehat z\) and \(\zeta(1,0,\mathbf1_p)\) are zero.  Therefore the total definitions satisfy
\[
 \widehat z=\zeta(\widehat\theta_n)
 =g_{\widehat r_n}(\widehat\xi_n)\quad\text{on }\mathcal V_n,
 \qquad
 \widehat z=\zeta(\widehat\theta_n)=0\quad\text{on }\mathcal V_n^c.
\tag{2}
\]

The contour-projector and polar-frame formulas (4)--(6) in the proof of \(\text{thm:rank-adaptive-estimation}\) show that the truncated active image has a differentiable local frame whenever the positive singular values are separated from zero.  In such a frame, \(F,q,\beta^\star,E,L^\star,H^\star,K^\star\), and \(Z^\star\) are compositions of multiplication, inversion at nonsingular matrices, the scalar logarithm on \((0,1)\), and a finite matrix polynomial.  Thus \(g_r\) is Fr\'{e}chet differentiable at each population point.  Identity (1) says that, on the open validity neighborhood, \(g_r=\zeta\circ\Phi_{\Delta,r}\circ\mathcal C\), including when a population signed-jump coordinate is zero.  This proves the differentiability claimed in the theorem; it neither requires nor asserts differentiability of either positive part separately.

The conditioning bounds (13)--(16) in \(\text{thm:rank-adaptive-estimation}\), \(\text{ass:rank-gap}\), \(\text{ass:decay-margin}\), \(\text{ass:parameter-envelope}\), and \(\text{ass:intensity-gap}\) give a common derivative bound and a common modulus of continuity.  There are only finitely many ranks.  Hence, on the uniformly likely event \(\{\widehat r_n=r(\theta)\}\cap\mathcal V_n\), Taylor expansion gives
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat z-\zeta(\theta)\}
 =J_z(\theta)\sqrt n\{\widehat\xi_n-\xi(\theta)\}+o_{P_\theta}(1),
 \qquad
 J_z(\theta)=D(\zeta\circ\Phi_{\Delta,r(\theta)}\circ\mathcal C)_{\xi(\theta)},
\tag{3}
\]
with a remainder uniform over \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)\).  Uniform rank and validity consistency follow from \(\text{thm:rank-adaptive-estimation}\).  Applying the bounded linear maps \(J_z(\theta)\) to the uniform Gaussian approximation in \(\text{lem:bin-moment-limit}\), then using (2)--(3), proves
\[
 \sup_{\theta:P_\theta\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}
 d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(
 \mathcal L_\theta[\sqrt n\{\zeta(\widehat\theta_n)-\zeta(\theta)\}],
 \mathcal N\{0,W(\theta)\}\right)\longrightarrow0,
\tag{4}
\]
where \(W(\theta)=J_z(\theta)\Omega(\theta)J_z(\theta)^{\mathsf T}\).

We next verify the covariance used for calibration.  Write \(v_s=Y_s-\overline Y_n\) and \(N_n=n-2\).  The Bartlett estimator in \(\text{def:hac-estimator}\) is exactly
\[
 \widehat\Omega_n=\frac1{N_n}\sum_{s,t=0}^{N_n-1}
 \left(1-\frac{|s-t|}{b_n}\right)_+v_sv_t^{\mathsf T}.
\tag{5}
\]
For integer \(b_n\geq1\),
\[
 \left(1-\frac{|s-t|}{b_n}\right)_+
 =\frac1{b_n}\sum_{\ell\in\mathbb Z}
 \mathbf1_{\{s\leq\ell<s+b_n\}}
 \mathbf1_{\{t\leq\ell<t+b_n\}},
\tag{6}
\]
a Gram representation.  Hence \(\widehat\Omega_n\succeq0\).  Its signed-score sandwich is positive semidefinite on \(\mathcal V_n\), and it is zero, hence positive semidefinite, on \(\mathcal V_n^c\).  By \(\text{lem:bin-moment-limit}\), \(\widehat\Omega_n\to\Omega(\theta)\) uniformly.  Derivative continuity, (3), and uniform validity then give, for every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 \sup_{\theta:P_\theta\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}
 P_\theta\{\lVert\widehat W_n-W(\theta)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}>\varepsilon\}
 \longrightarrow0.
\tag{7}
\]

The accepted optional full-parameter object is also fully explicit.  The event
\[
 \mathcal D_n=\mathcal V_n\cap
 \{Z_{ij}^\star\neq0\text{ for every }1\leq i<j\leq p\}
\tag{8}
\]
is measurable: \(\mathcal V_n\) is measurable by \(\text{def:rank-adaptive-estimator}\), every starred map is Borel on it, and (8) is a finite intersection of inverse images of \(\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}\).  On \(\mathcal D_n\), every positive-part coordinate is differentiable and the full sandwich \(\widehat V_n\) is defined; on \(\mathcal D_n^c\) it is the declared zero placeholder and the optional parameter set uses its full-space fallback.  Neither object enters (4) or graph calibration.

It remains to justify calibration when \(W(\theta)\) is singular.  Define the raw-moment direction
\[
 v_\theta=\{0,\operatorname{vec}(\Gamma_1),\operatorname{vec}(\Gamma_2)\}.
\]
Along \(\xi+s v_\theta\), the mean is fixed and both centered lag covariances are multiplied by \(1+s\).  Thus the active image is fixed, \(R\) is multiplied by \(1+s\), and direct cancellation in the formula for \(F\) gives \(F(s)=F\).  Consequently \(q,E,L^\star,H^\star\) are fixed while \(K^\star,Z^\star\), and \(g_r\) are multiplied by \(1+s\).  Therefore
\[
 J_z(\theta)v_\theta=\zeta(\theta).
\tag{9}
\]
The moment envelope gives \(\lVert v_\theta\rVert_2\leq C_0\).  Since the support is nonempty and \(\text{ass:edge-gap}\) holds, some coordinate \(a=a(\theta)\) has \(|\zeta_a(\theta)|\geq\kappa\).  If \(j_a\) is the corresponding row of \(J_z(\theta)\), (9) implies \(\lVert j_a\rVert_2\geq\kappa/C_0\).  By \(\text{ass:variance-gap}\),
\[
 W_{aa}(\theta)=j_a\Omega(\theta)j_a^{\mathsf T}
 \geq\kappa\lVert j_a\rVert_2^2
 \geq c_\star:=\kappa^3/C_0^2>0.
\tag{10}
\]
The uniform derivative and long-run-variance bounds also give \(\lVert W(\theta)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\leq C_1\).

Let \(G\sim\mathcal N(0,W(\theta))\) and \(M=\max_{1\leq a\leq d}|G_a|\).  For \(0<\varepsilon<1\) and \(x\geq0\), if \(x\leq\sqrt\varepsilon\), (10) and the bounded density of its nondegenerate coordinate give
\[
 P(x<M\leq x+\varepsilon)
 \leq P\{|G_a|\leq\sqrt\varepsilon+\varepsilon\}
 \leq C_2\sqrt\varepsilon.
\]
If \(x>\sqrt\varepsilon\), the event requires at least one coordinate absolute value to lie in \((x,x+\varepsilon]\).  For a centered normal coordinate of variance \(s^2>0\), its absolute-value density at \(y>0\), maximized over \(s\), is at most \(C/y\); a zero-variance coordinate contributes zero.  A union bound gives
\[
 \sup_{\theta}\sup_{x\geq0}P_\theta(x<M\leq x+\varepsilon)
 \leq C_3d\sqrt\varepsilon.
\tag{11}
\]
Thus the Gaussian-maximum laws have a uniform continuous modulus despite possible singular covariance.

For a positive semidefinite matrix \(V\), set
\[
 F_V(x)=P\!\left\{\max_{a\leq d}|(V^{1/2}U)_a|\leq x\right\},
 \qquad U\sim\mathcal N(0,I_d),
\]
and use the generalized-inverse convention
\[
 c(V;1-\alpha)=\inf\{x\in[0,\infty):F_V(x)\geq1-\alpha\},
 \qquad \inf\varnothing=+\infty.
\tag{12}
\]
This defines the conditional critical value even for singular \(V\).  On the operator-norm bounded positive-semidefinite set, the square-root map is uniformly continuous: this follows by diagonalizing two matrices, approximating \(x\mapsto\sqrt x\) uniformly by polynomials on the common spectral interval, and using continuity of each polynomial.  Coupling \(\widehat W_n^{1/2}U\) and \(W(\theta)^{1/2}U\), then applying (7), (11), and Markov's inequality to \(\lVert U\rVert_2\), proves
\[
 \sup_{x\geq0}|F_{\widehat W_n}(x)-F_{W(\theta)}(x)|=o_{P_\theta}(1)
\tag{13}
\]
uniformly on \(\mathcal V_n\).

Let \(c_{n,1-\alpha}=c(\widehat W_n;1-\alpha)\), exactly as in the corrected \(\text{def:graph-confidence-set}\).  On the event that the left side of (13) is at most \(\delta\), the generalized-inverse definition implies
\[
 c_{n,1-\alpha}\geq
 \inf\{x:F_{W(\theta)}(x)\geq1-\alpha-\delta\}.
\tag{14}
\]
The vector bounded-Lipschitz approximation (4), with upper and lower Lipschitz approximations to the maximum rectangle and boundary error bounded by (11), applies at the deterministic threshold on the right of (14).  Letting first \(n\to\infty\) and then \(\delta\downarrow0\) yields
\[
 \inf_{\theta:P_\theta\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}
 P_\theta\!\left[
 \max_{i<j}\left|\sqrt n\{\widehat z_{ij}-\zeta_{ij}(\theta)\}\right|
 \leq c_{n,1-\alpha},\ \mathcal V_n\right]
 \geq1-\alpha-o(1)-\sup_\theta P_\theta(\mathcal V_n^c).
\tag{15}
\]
On \(\mathcal V_n^c\), every interval is \(\mathbb R\), so simultaneous coordinate coverage is automatic.  Combining this fallback with (15) and uniform validity proves
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\theta:P_\theta\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}
 P_\theta\{\zeta_{ij}(\theta)\in I_{ij,n}\text{ for all }i<j\}
 \geq1-\alpha.
\tag{16}
\]

Finally, nonnegative excitation and acyclicity imply that at most one of \(A_{ij}\) and \(A_{ji}\) is positive.  Since every \(\lambda_i>0\), \(\zeta_{ij}>0\) means \(j\to i\), \(\zeta_{ij}<0\) means \(i\to j\), and \(\zeta_{ij}=0\) means neither edge.  On the event in (16), every true pairwise choice is admitted by the sign-inversion rules, and the true graph is acyclic; hence it belongs to \(\mathcal C_n(1-\alpha)\).  On \(\mathcal V_n^c\), that set contains every labeled acyclic graph.  Therefore
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\theta:P_\theta\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}
 P_\theta\{G(A)\in\mathcal C_n(1-\alpha)\}\geq1-\alpha.
\]

Construct a data-only \(\mathfrak U_n=(\mathcal G_n,\mathcal T_n)\in\mathfrak H_{n,\kappa_0}(\alpha)\) uniformly over the same nuisance-regular closure \(\overline{\mathcal M}_{\Delta,p}(\kappa_0)\), and characterize the sharp frontier \(\mathfrak R_{n,\kappa_0}(\delta_n)=(R_{G,n,\kappa_0}(\delta_n),R_{\Theta,n,\kappa_0}(\delta_n))\) for every sequence \(\delta_n\downarrow0\). statements.statement: For every law in \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{stab}}\), \(B\) is a real Hurwitz matrix, \(Q\succ0\), \(C_{+}(t)=e^{Bt}K\) for \(t>0\), \(K=A(2\beta I_p-A)Q\), \(K-K^{\mathsf T}=AD-DA^{\mathsf T}\), and \(\Gamma_k=T^{k-1}J^2K\) for every \(k\geq1\). Moreover, \(J\) is invertible, \(\operatorname{im}(\Gamma_1)=\operatorname{im}(K)=\operatorname{im}(A)\), and \(\operatorname{rank}(\Gamma_1)=\operatorname{rank}(A)\).
